mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen steadily for three consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC has fallen, indicating a substitution of time-at-home for discretionary outings. This substitution effect persists mechanically, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining at or above its t-0w level, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has crossed a severe-contraction threshold of -20 points for two consecutive weeks, a level historically associated with active transit restrictions or public avoidance under lockdown orders. This policy-linked transit suppression propagates to retail access within two weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -20 points for two consecutive weekly means
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -21.3 and -20.7 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while TRANSIT remains below -20, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT compound each other: reduced commuting (WORKPLACES down) combined with reduced transit usage (TRANSIT down) jointly removes the incidental retail trips normally bundled with commuting, producing a larger-than-additive drop in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined sharply from t-3w to t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC decline over the next two weeks is no larger than the sum of the individual historical sensitivities to WORKPLACES and TRANSIT changes, the interaction effect is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The current snapshot reflects a tightening-restrictions regime, evidenced by concurrent sharp declines in PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES alongside rising RESIDENTIAL. Under such a regime, discretionary retail and recreation activity continues to contract as restrictions bind, so RETAIL_REC will trend lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while PARKS, TRANSIT, and WORKPLACES remain depressed and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, the regime-conditional mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC improved from -17.3 to -14.4 in the most recent week, the first weekly improvement in the series, suggesting a near-term bottoming of the contraction. This single-week momentum reversal typically precedes a short continuation of modest recovery in the following week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC improves week-on-week after at least two prior weeks of decline
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -17.3 at t-1w to -14.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC falls again below -17.3 in the following week, the momentum-reversal mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained flat (near 0) while RETAIL_REC has fallen sharply, showing the public continues essential shopping but actively avoids discretionary retail and recreation venues. This divergence reflects a persistent risk-avoidance behavior pattern that keeps RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near 0 while RETAIL_REC fell to -14.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC recovers toward baseline while the GROCERY_PHARM-RETAIL_REC gap does not narrow, the avoidance-behavior mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded sharply from -18.9 to -5.3 in the latest week, likely reflecting a seasonal or weather-driven resurgence in outdoor activity. This renewed outdoor mobility often spills over into nearby retail and recreation foot traffic as people combine outings, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -18.9 at t-1w to -5.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above -10, the seasonal-spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint stabilization of RESIDENTIAL at a high plateau (~6.3-6.4) alongside the PARKS rebound and the slight WORKPLACES recovery (-6.9 to -7.7 narrowing from -10.1) signals an early reopening regime where restrictions are easing. Under this regime, RETAIL_REC should begin recovering over the next four weeks as pent-up discretionary demand is released.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL plateaued near 6.3-6.4 while PARKS and WORKPLACES improved at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to fall over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated and PARKS/WORKPLACES do not sustain their improvement, the reopening mechanism is rejected.
